description: Remove payload zero-fill before overwrite; TCP prepends headers into reserved space. Release HVF comparison including all slow samples.
interpretation: No large speedup established. Candidate first virtio run had multi-second slow transfers, but its repeat returned to previous throughput. Previous image also had slow NCM transfers. A non-task rustc process and macOS background CPU activity were observed during measurements; effects are not isolated. All samples are retained, without excluding slow transfers. Final separate NCM checks show original RX 763.77 Mbps versus candidate 813.24 Mbps; TX medians are both ~352.65 Mbps. This is not a controlled estimate of the zero-fill contribution.
remaining_candidates: ACK processing scans retained segments and replaces retransmission timers when the head changes.
Packet-level worker wake/queue latency; slow transfers show more guest idle time, not proportional growth in CPU work.
SLiRP and software device backend costs; no Linux guest reference establishes this setup maximum.

post_measurement_correction.description: Ethernet ARP miss now forwards PacketBuffer directly to queue_owned_packet_on_interface instead of compacting into Vec before adoption. Measurements precede this final call-site correction; no throughput effect claimed.
